topic: How does frequency overlap between GPS L1 and Galileo E1 impact interference mitigation in multi-GNSS receiver link budgets?
consensus_response: Frequency overlap between GPS L1 and Galileo E1 leads to increased interference, compromising multi-GNSS receiver link budgets. The physical mechanism behind this phenomenon is the array factor, which depends on antenna spacing and radiation pattern. Advanced signal processing techniques like blind source separation (BSS) or machine learning-based algorithms can improve interference mitigation by exploiting frequency diversity. However, these techniques increase complexity and power consumption due to the need for more sophisticated receiver architectures.
